summary: Backend regression testing for CreatorGuard AI Gmail OAuth hardening + Claude analyze. All 8 pytest tests PASSED in 10s. Callback hardening verified: /api/oauth/gmail/callback now handles ?error=access_denied and no-params cases with 307 redirects to FRONTEND_URL (gmail=error&reason=...) instead of 422s. Bogus state still correctly returns 400. Login endpoint returns proper authorize_url with all required scopes + offline/consent. Status/settings endpoints work and persist. Claude Sonnet 4.5 analyze endpoint returns full structured verdict — no regression from Gmail changes.
critical_code_review_comments: logger is used in server.py analyze() but logging.basicConfig + logger = getLogger are declared AFTER the router include; on module import the logger works because Python resolves globals lazily, but the basicConfig call happens after uvicorn may have already configured logging. Cosmetic only.

gmail_integration.py fetch_token warning suppression is fine but note google-auth-oauthlib scope-order warning could indicate scope drift if Google adds a new scope automatically; consider logging the mismatch.

Callback redirect on error is unsigned/public — anyone can hit /api/oauth/gmail/callback?error=foo to trigger a redirect. This is expected behavior for OAuth callbacks (Google itself is the caller), no action needed.
test_credentials: None required — EMERGENT_LLM_KEY and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET already in backend/.env
seed_data_creation: Test uses random UUID-based user_ids per test to avoid state collisions; no persistent seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_creatorguard_backend.py covers OAuth callback hardening, login authorize_url, gmail status/settings, and Claude analyze regression. Uses INTERNAL_BASE=http://localhost:8001. Full OAuth completion (real Google login → callback with code) cannot be tested without a browser + real Google account; the user's Google Console 'Access blocked / test user' issue is a Google Cloud Console config on their side, not a backend bug. Backend now correctly handles the error path when Google redirects with ?error=access_denied.
rca of the issue: Original 422 on /api/oauth/gmail/callback was caused by required Query params (code, state) — when Google redirected back with only ?error=access_denied, FastAPI rejected the request with 422 Unprocessable Entity. Fix (already applied by E1): made code/state/error all Optional[str]=None in the callback signature and added explicit branches that redirect to FRONTEND_URL with gmail=error&reason=<code> when error is present, or reason=missing_params when both code and state are absent. Verified via test_callback_with_only_error_param_redirects (307 + Location contains gmail=error&reason=access_denied) and test_callback_with_no_params_redirects.
